journeys.claim: A launch draws the fleet this phone remembers before it has reached anything, every row shimmering and nothing spinning, and a real connection to two real hosts confirms it. Today that confirmation leaves the list empty: pairing from the phone is not built, so neither machine vouches for anything this phone remembered. That a row goes solid when its own host answers, without the list moving, is proven where it happens — in the shared library's cache tests and the fleet store's — and becomes a claim about the screen here once a paired phone can be driven through this journey.

Six agents on two machines the runner is running, on a phone that pairs with both of them through the protocol itself: before it has reached anything the phone draws the ones it remembers, the two that need an answer at the top and the one waiting longest first; a real connection reaches both machines and every remembered row goes solid where it stands as its own machine answers for it, a turn emitted by one of them changes nothing about the order, and taking the relay away leaves every row on screen under the one line that says the phone is offline; a phone that remembers nothing shows the home empty; and opening the row at the top reaches the whole fleet from a drawer over the conversation and comes back.

A phone paired with the machine that holds them opens one of its agents and reads what it says: every kind of step the scripted provider can play arrives over the relay and is drawn, a folded run of reads opens when it is pressed, a diff the host computed puts the changes chip on screen and it leads to the changes, and an agent that ends while somebody is reading it states its code and offers nowhere to write. Losing the machine says so where the composer will go, with a way to ask again. Three messages tried where the conversation will not take one — in the moment it opens and the layer is still catching up, while the machine is unreachable, and while the last one is unanswered — are refused on the phone with the reason on screen, and the host confirms it received only the single message that was allowed through.

Everything an agent can be waiting to be told, answered on the phone against a machine the runner is really running: a permission refused and another allowed, the standing grant the host itself offered taken by the name the host gave it, the agent's own question answered with one of the agent's own answers, a plan read out and approved and a second sent back with what should change, a plan judged earlier reopened onto the document that was judged, an agent this one started answered in its own conversation and the provider's own subagent saying why it has none, and a finished turn deferred and then read. The host is asked afterwards what it received, and every answer is exactly what was pressed.

A patch a real host froze, read as one scroll and written about with a finger: ranges taken by holding a line and dragging, three remarks added and a fourth cancelled before it was said, and the whole review attached and sent with a remark about the change as a whole. The host received one message carrying that patch's identity, those ranges, what was said about each of them and the patch pinned to it — and nothing about the remark that was cancelled.

Writing to two agents the runner is really running. A paragraph typed over two lines; a long paste, a stored photograph, a stored file and a patch the machine computed each standing in that sentence as one token at the caret; one backspace taking a whole token entire, and one token taken from between two others and put in front of both — whole, as the one character it is in the sentence. That move goes through the field's own draft rather than a finger: the gesture that performs it on a device is the text view's own text drag, which the system begins from drawn text and no driver outside the process can start. One message sent, drawn before the machine answered for it and still one row once it had. One message held while a turn ran, replaced by a second, taken back into the field, and a third that survived the turn being stopped and was delivered when the turn ended — the machine's own account says it received exactly those two and nothing that was replaced or withdrawn. The cross empties the field and leaves the turn running; Stop is offered only where there is nothing to send, so no press does both. The address copied, a rename cancelled and then kept by the machine, a deletion cancelled and later confirmed. And on the session that offers them: a command raised by a slash, sent as a token and answered, and a model and an effort changed and read back off the chip the machine's own facts relabel.

New Agent creates Claude on the SDK driver, confirmed by the daemon inventory with no PTY agent created. The created SDK agent and pre-existing SDK and PTY agents open under their original identities, render through their own projections, and each round-trip a prompt observed by the host. A typed model change reaches the SDK session; the PTY gate refuses it with no extra input. A creation the host refuses leaves a designed failure state and creates nothing.

What this phone's link to two machines the runner is running does over time: a relay taken away and put back is recovered from with nobody pressing anything; each machine holds one connection however many conversations are open, and nothing is asked of them while the phone sits idle; pressing Retry Now reaches the link before the relay is back, which is the only thing that could have; putting the phone away releases the link so the machines see it leave, and bringing it back confirms the fleet again; and the conversation closed before any of it holds no stream after all of it.

Giving a phone machines to work on, and keeping two accounts apart, against three machines the runner is really running. A pairing link the launch itself carried lands on a phone nobody has signed in on and trusts nothing; signing in puts it to the machine, which answers with its own name and the whole of its key; turned down it still holds no key, and the same invitation — the machine is still offering it — is opened again and agreed to. On the keypad, a code nobody issued and a code that has run out are refused in one sentence with the digits gone, and the code the machine printed leads to that machine's name and key before any trust is written. Three agents are started on one machine — from a directory it had been used in, from a repository it listed, and from a path typed by hand, with a path it refuses saying so and starting nothing — and the machine itself reports every one of them as Claude on the SDK driver, with no terminal Claude session appearing anywhere; the one the phone started opens as the SDK layer's own typed state and the one the topology seeded still opens as a transcript. A key read whole on the phone is revoked while one of that machine's agents is open, and the access it carried ends at once: the stream that conversation was reading is let go and everything the machine was running leaves the fleet. The relay is taken away and put back and a machine restarted underneath, and the phone recovers with nobody pressing anything. And the second account on the same phone reaches only its own machine, pairs with it under an identity of its own, and sees none of the first account's.

One phone, one sitting, and everything a person does about the account it reaches its machines with. It opens on the real home, empty, with one thing to do and no account; the hand-off names where it is sending you and never asks for a password, and is refused in the account service's own words, cancelled without leaving anything to dismiss, and finished with nothing bought. Both subscriptions are pressed at the App Store: a sheet closed without buying leaves the same plan chosen, a refusal says what the store said, one left waiting for approval says nothing has been charged and stops offering to buy, restoring nothing says so, and the one that goes through is carried to the account service before it is finished with the store. A purchase amux.sh is never told about is kept and offered again; one it refuses reads differently; sent again and taken, what the account may do is read back rather than believed. Restoring on a phone with nothing bought takes the same road, and a purchase the store approves by itself reaches the account service with nobody pressing anything. A second account is added from the same page, keeps the phone where it was, and is honoured with the subscription it bought on the web — the screen says where it came from instead of selling a second one. Each account pairs with its own machine on a real relay under an identity of its own and sees only its own agents; with one on screen the other still says what it has waiting, from its own live subscription, and an answer that account's connection had already produced arriving after the switch is refused and changes nothing. An account signed out of stays listed with Sign In beside it and comes back with a subscription that has since ended. Delete Account states what goes, refuses to unlock until the account's own address is typed, is refused while the subscription is still set to renew — naming the only place that can be stopped and keeping the address typed across the trip there — and then takes the account off the phone. Light, Dark and System each redraw the whole app under the thumb, and Contact Support leaves for the web. Nothing here reaches a real account service or a real App Store: both are doubles handed to the app at launch, which is what makes a refused purchase, a purchase waiting for approval and a refused deletion states a finger can reach.

Reporting what went wrong on a phone paired with a machine the runner is really running, so the picture in every report is a screen that machine filled. The system photographs the app and the app's own Report appears — a hundred points clear of the corner the system draws its thumbnail preview in, because no app is given that preview to attach anything to — and anywhere else on the screen turns it down and lets the frozen frame go. With the other preview setting the system covers the app entirely; put away and brought back, the same offer over the same frozen frame is still there. Taking it opens the report on the frame frozen when the offer appeared, with no share step, no sheet and nothing asked of Photos — the build asks for no access to the photo library at all, so what it draws cannot be the picture the system saved. Three rectangles are dragged onto the picture, each takes a note and one more is written about the whole thing. The account service turns the report down in its own words, nothing written is lost, and Retry hands over the same bundle again and comes back with a receipt. What left the phone is opened where it crossed that boundary: every part is declared present with the file beside it or absent with the reason, the rectangles and both notes are carried, and the frame is the whole screen in points with the scale it was drawn at. Report a Problem under Help does the same deliberately, with no offer in between, and its bundle names the page it was pressed on rather than the one the screenshot was taken on. Nothing here reaches amux.sh: the account service is a double the app is handed at launch, which is what makes a refused upload a state a finger can reach.

Everything a person mainly does with this app, done again with the accessibility settings on: VoiceOver running on the device and the whole app drawn at the largest text size a reader can ask for, against two machines the runner is really running. The app itself says it is in a VoiceOver session and says what size it is drawn at, so neither is taken on trust. At that size the fleet still lists its agents and every action it offers has a name to read out; a conversation still reads, and the patch its machine froze still gives up a range to a finger held on one line and dragged onto the next; a permission is refused and a plan approved with the panel's own controls, and the sheet that asks what should change is got out of without answering it; a token pasted into the message stands in the sentence as one character and one backspace takes the whole of it, and the card that renames the agent is opened and cancelled; the machines are listed; and a machine taken away while somebody is reading one of its agents says the same thing in light and in dark. What each screen drew, and how far the actions it is for sit from the bottom of the window, is written out beside the photographs.
